steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The central purpose of economic activity is the production of goods and services to satisfy needs (essentials) and wants (desirables). | Key Fact: The three key economic decisions: what to produce, how to produce, and who is to benefit from production. | Key Fact: The three main economic groups are consumers (buy goods/services), producers (make goods/services), and government (regulates and provides public services). | Key Fact: Goods are tangible products (food, clothing); services are intangible (healthcare, education). Both satisfy needs and wants.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between a need and a want, giving two examples of each. | Describe the three key economic decisions that all societies must make. | Analyse how the three main economic groups interact in a market economy.
